definitions.explanation: The hidden side of society where criminal and illicit activities take place. Encompasses organized crime, black markets, and illegal networks operating outside the law.

examples.japanese: {裏社会|うらしゃかい}とのつながりが{発覚|はっかく}した。
examples.english: His connections to the underworld were exposed.

examples.japanese: その{映画|えいが}は{裏社会|うらしゃかい}の{実態|じったい}を{描|えが}いている。
examples.english: That movie depicts the reality of the underworld.

examples.japanese: {警察|けいさつ}は{裏社会|うらしゃかい}に{流|なが}れる{資金|しきん}のルートを{追|お}っている。
examples.english: The police are tracking the flow of funds into the underworld.

notes:
Literally "back society" or "reverse-side society." The prefix {裏|うら} (back, hidden side) contrasts with {表|おもて} (front, public side), reflecting the idea of a hidden world operating behind the visible surface of society. Frequently encountered in crime fiction, news reports, and documentaries.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {裏社会|うらしゃかい}の{人間|にんげん}: people from the underworld
- {裏社会|うらしゃかい}とのつながり: connections to the underworld
- {裏社会|うらしゃかい}に{足|あし}を{踏|ふ}み{入|い}れる: to set foot in the underworld
- {裏社会|うらしゃかい}を{牛耳|ぎゅうじ}る: to control the underworld

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {闇社会|やみしゃかい}: dark society — nearly synonymous, slightly more dramatic
- {暗黒街|あんこくがい}: dark streets — emphasizes specific criminal districts
- {犯罪組織|はんざいそしき}: criminal organization — refers to specific groups rather than the broader world
